AccountOpening.description:
When a mock account opened, at its first read or its last reset, and the cash it opened with. Its account page, the
equity curve and the trades start there. A real broker reports none.

AiModelResponse.description: My settings' AI model: the models the site offers its users, its default among them, and the one the user's runs use.
AiModelResponse.title: AiModelResponse

ArchiveStatusResponse.description:
The open-data archive's warm-up. A public site reads its daily history from the archive alone, so its runs find no

Arithmetic-Input.description:
Two numbers combined: `{"type": "arithmetic", "operator": "multiply", "left": <25-day average volume>,
"right": 1.8}` is 1.8 times that average. Either side may be another arithmetic part.

Two numbers combined: `{"type": "arithmetic", "operator": "multiply", "left": <25-day average volume>,

AttributedProvider.description: An agency whose open data the app reads, by the name it publishes under, and the names of the datasets it reads.

Audience.description:
Whom the deployment serves, and with it which data and brokers it may use. Its properties are the one table of
what each audience allows; the wiring, the trading setup check and the gates of the Web API and the CLI read them,

AudienceResponse.description:
Whom the site serves and what that allows, as the Audience table says, so the web app offers only what the site can

AuthStatusResponse.description: What the web app shows first: the first-time setup, or sign-in with or without registration.

BacktestInputs.description: What a user chooses for one backtest: the period, the cash it starts with and the scores that buy and sell.

buy_score.description: A stock that passes the strategy with at least this score is bought: analysis.min_combined_score_buy in a run.

last.description: The backtest covers every session from `first` to `last`, both included.

sell_score.description: A held stock at or below this score is sold: analysis.max_combined_score_sell in a run.

BacktestTrade.description:
One position of a backtest from its first BUY to its SELL, or to the backtest's last session when it is still held
then. Later BUYs of a held stock add to the same trade. Every field is in every answer, so the Web API's schema
requires each one.

average_cost.description: Per share, the buy fees included, as Position.average_cost.

bought_on.description: The session of the first BUY.
bought_on.title: Bought On

fee.description: The broker fees paid: every BUY's, and the SELL's once sold.

held_sessions.description: Sessions from the first BUY to the SELL, or to the last session.

pnl.description:
Net of every fee and the tax (Position.profit_on_sale). For a trade still open, what selling it at the last
session's close would bring.
pnl.title: Pnl

return_pct.description: The PnL as a fraction of what the shares cost.
return_pct.title: Return Pct

sold_at.description: The SELL's fill price. None while the trade is still open at the last session.

Breadth.description:
How many stocks rose, fell and closed unchanged in one session, and their average change in percent, each stock
weighing the same.

A broker the signed-in user may choose for a run now, as a run's confirmation names it: the mock account always,

ExplanationRequest.description: One AI call explains one stock's valuation; the numbers are the domain's, the AI writes only text.

FollowItem.description: One follow of a decision: the follow's decision, priced when it was followed, and its order.

ListedStockResponse.title: ListedStockResponse

MarketField.description: A field of one completed daily bar. Volume is in shares.
MarketField.title: MarketField

MarketIndex.description: A market index with a daily history: the own index of the exchange `market` names, kept under that market.

MarketValue.description:
A field of one completed daily bar, `bars_ago` trading days before the latest one.
`{"type": "market", "field": "volume", "bars_ago": 1}` is yesterday's volume in shares.
MarketValue.title: MarketValue

MonthlyRevenue.description:
One company's revenue of one month, as the TWSE or TPEX OpenAPI's monthly revenue summary serves it, under the

Ohlcv.description:
One bar of trading. A daily bar is stamped at its session's 13:30 close in Asia/Taipei, and its volume is in shares.
Every field is in every answer, so the Web API's schema requires each one.

change.description:
The exchange's official change from the session's reference price: the previous close, adjusted on an ex-rights or
ex-dividend day. The exchanges' daily reports and listings and the broker's snapshots report it; a bar without one,
or whose exchange compared its close to no reference, has None.

Ohlcv.title: Ohlcv

OpenDataAttribution.description:
The credit the Open Government Data License v1 asks of every use, in the form of its annex: each providing agency
with its datasets, the license's notice, and the license's name and address. A use that does not give it holds no
license from the start (Article 3, paragraph 2), so a page that shows open data shows this too.
OpenDataAttribution.title: OpenDataAttribution

Order.description:
The app's record of one order: the decision it executes, what went to (or was refused before)
the broker, and how it ended. OrderPreparation saves it in the `orders` table before it is sent, and OrderExecution
saves the broker's answer, whichever provider ran it.

What prices an order of this deployment, in which phase of the trading day it may be placed and on which brokers.
Audience.order_pricing picks one; OrderGateRule and the follow's window read it, and nothing else decides by it.
OrderPricing.title: OrderPricing

OrderStatus.description: Order lifecycle. Each status lists the statuses that may follow it in next_statuses.
OrderStatus.title: OrderStatus

Permission.description:
What a role may do beyond using its own data. A signed-in user of any role runs every workflow on their own mock
account, watchlist, records and strategies; no permission is needed for that. Each member's docstring names where

ProblemsResponse.description: Settings the app would not start with (`settings_refused`): nothing was saved; the problems say where and why.

One company's figures of one quarter, as its balance sheet, its income statement and its EPS statistics in the TWSE

RunReference.description: Which run a trade came from, as the account page names it.

SettingChange.description: One setting the settings form changes: the path of its field, and its new value as JSON.

else null; its options and bounds from the settings classes; and whether it applies only at a restart.
SettingField.title: SettingField

SettingKind.description: How the administrator's settings form shows a setting and takes its new value.
SettingKind.title: SettingKind

SettingsFile.description: A settings file in config/ the administrator may edit from the Web. Nothing else on disk can be named.
SettingsFile.title: SettingsFile

SettingsProblem.description:
One reason the app would not start with the settings: what, and where when a settings file names a place. The

pydantic's own text can quote the input, which can be a secret from .env.

SetupRequest.description: The first administrator, with the one-time code the server printed on its console at start.
SetupRequest.title: SetupRequest

SignalResponse.description: A trading decision (TradeSignal) and its evidence; the AI report leaves out the model's raw answer.

SignalSource.title: SignalSource

StockFinancialsResponse.description:
A stock's financials as the server's open-data archive holds them. The OpenAPI serves only the latest quarter and
month, so the archive holds those it saved while they were served, and nothing before the archive started.
StockFinancialsResponse.title: StockFinancialsResponse

StockReportResponse.description: One requested stock after a specific-stock analysis (StockReport), as the CLI's Stock Reports table shows it.
StockReportResponse.title: StockReportResponse

StockValuationResponse.description: One stock's valuation before any user assumption (StockValuation).
StockValuationResponse.title: StockValuationResponse

TechnicalReport.description:
Result produced by a TechnicalStrategy.

Hard failures reject the stock.
Soft failures reduce technical quality without rejecting the stock.
Observations describe optional technical signals.
TechnicalReport.title: TechnicalReport

TechnicalRule-Input.description: A condition and what passing or failing it does to the score. The name is a label: the condition alone decides.
TechnicalRule-Input.title: TechnicalRule

TechnicalRule-Output.description: A condition and what passing or failing it does to the score. The name is a label: the condition alone decides.
TechnicalRule-Output.title: TechnicalRule

TechnicalScoring.description:
Each rule's effect applies once, however many conditions it holds: a failed block_on_fail rule rejects the stock
and costs block_failure_penalty, a failed reduce_score_on_fail rule costs failure_score_reduction, and a passed

One owner's strategies and the active one, which every workflow uses. revision counts the owner's saves, so a save
from an older read is refused instead of overwriting.

TechnicalSettings-Output.description:
One owner's strategies and the active one, which every workflow uses. revision counts the owner's saves, so a save
from an older read is refused instead of overwriting.
TechnicalSettings-Output.title: TechnicalSettings

The user's formulas over named indicators, scored together. strategy_id is a stable key and name a label. An

The user's formulas over named indicators, scored together. strategy_id is a stable key and name a label. An
indicator id such as ind_a never holds a parameter: changing ind_a's period changes every rule that reads ind_a,
and a rule that needs a different period reads another indicator.
TechnicalStrategy-Output.title: TechnicalStrategy

TimeInForce.description: How long an accepted order keeps working (Taiwan exchange terms).
TimeInForce.title: TimeInForce

TradeResponse.description: An order that filled at least one share, and the run whose decision it carried out: the followed run for a follow.
TradeResponse.title: TradeResponse

User.description:
A person who signs in, and the owner of their own mock account, watchlist, records and strategies. It holds no
credential: the user store keeps the password hash and the encrypted username and email, and hands back this model
with both decrypted, so the Web answers with it.

permissions.description: What the user's role allows beyond their own data: the web app shows the administration pages from it.
permissions.title: Permissions

User.title: User

UserChangeRequest.description: An administrator's change of one user. A field left out stays as it is.
UserChangeRequest.title: UserChangeRequest

ValuationReportResponse.description: A stock valued at the user's target P/E (ValuationReport). Scenarios exist exactly when its P/E is computable.
ValuationReportResponse.title: ValuationReportResponse

Workflow.description: The user-facing operation a run belongs to. Each run has one run id.
Workflow.title: Workflow

APIKeyCookie.description: The session POST /v1/auth/sign-in sets: HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/v1, Secure over https.
APIKeyCookie.name: stock_agent_session

info.description:
Runs the stock-agent workflows and reads what they recorded, on the same runtime as the CLI.

Users. Anyone may register (`POST /v1/auth/register`) while registration is open, and signs in with a username or an
email (`POST /v1/auth/sign-in`), which sets the HttpOnly session cookie `stock_agent_session`. Public: sign-in,
registration, the first-time setup, the built-in strategies and market data (`/v1/market`). Signed in: every other
read and write, each on the user's own runs, decisions, orders, watchlist, mock account and saved technical settings.
Administrator: the users (`/v1/admin/users`) and the settings form (`/v1/admin/settings`). 401 means sign in: the
session is missing, expired or ended. 403 means signed in but not allowed, and never ends the session. Every write
sends the header `X-Requested-With: stock-agent`, and every write but sign-in, sign-out, registration and setup
repeats `"confirm": true` in its body.

Orders. Full Cycle, specific-stock analysis, valuation and market data never order. Buzz, Intraday and a manual BUY
of a stock a specific-stock run reported (`POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/manual-buy`) send orders through the same gates and
trading journal as the CLI, on the broker their `broker` query names for the whole run: the user's mock account by
default, or SinoPac (`shioaji`) for an administrator while the site's Shioaji login is up, on its simulation server
in dev and test and on the real account in prod, each BUY within trading.max_order_value and the day's within
trading.max_daily_buy_value (`GET /v1/account/brokers` names them). A follow (`POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/follow`) places a
finished Full Cycle's open decisions in the user's mock account only, priced again: at a fresh realtime quote in
continuous trading, or on a site without realtime quotes at the last session's official close while no session
trades. No endpoint cancels or modifies an order.

Open data. A public site (`audience: public`) uses only the TWSE and TPEX OpenAPI data the server archives: daily
history and the index trend come from that archive, it has no realtime quote, so Buzz and Intraday answer 403
`realtime_quotes_unavailable`, and it trades on the mock broker only. A personal site reads its daily history and
index trend from the exchanges' own daily reports; without a Shioaji login it has no realtime quote either, so it
answers Buzz and Intraday the same way. A public site reads no news site and no MOPS: the AI step
reads the archived material information, the TWSE news naming the stock and its archived financials, a stock with none
of them is decided on its technical score alone, and every valuation endpoint answers 403 `mops_unavailable`. `GET
/v1/market/audience` answers the site's audience and what it allows, so the web app offers only that. `GET
/v1/market/archive-status` says how many sessions the archive holds and how many the built-in strategies need, `GET
/v1/market/stocks/{stock_id}/financials` answers a stock's archived quarters and monthly revenue, and `GET
/v1/market/attribution` names the open data's providers, datasets and license, which a page showing it must credit.

Backtests. `POST /v1/backtests` replays the user's active technical strategy over past sessions the site already
holds, with the live trading rules on the technical score alone, and saves the result for the user (`GET
/v1/backtests`, `GET /v1/backtests/{backtest_id}`). `GET /v1/backtests/options` names the period it may cover. A
backtest asks no AI, touches no account, watchlist or run record, and never orders.

Workflows run in the background, one at a time per user and a few at a time per server: a start answers 202 with the
run id, and GET /v1/runs/{run_id} reports the run's state and its record; another user's run id answers 404. Run the
server with one worker process.
info.title: TW-Stock-Alpha-Agent

get.description:
The brokers the user may choose for Buzz, Intraday or a manual BUY now, the mock account first, each with what a
run's confirmation names: a real broker's server and its BUY limits.

schema.title: Response Get Brokers V1 Account Brokers Get

get.description:
Menu 7 on the `broker` account, the mock account by default: the account now, its equity curve, and the account at
the end of `as_of`. It never orders and records no run.

403.description: real_broker_refused: a real broker's account, asked by a user who is not an administrator. broker_unavailable: the real broker has no login up on this site now.

post.description:
Opens the user's mock account again with `initial_cash` and no positions; its equity curve and trades start anew
and every decision is open to follow again. No run, decision or order is deleted. 409 while a run of the user
runs, which could order on the account meanwhile.

409.description: run_in_progress: a run of the user is still running.

get.description:
Every order of a run on the `broker` account (the mock account by default) that filled at least one share, since
the mock account opened or every one at a real broker, newest first, each with the run whose decision it carried
out: a follow's with the run it followed. Ask for limit + 1 to know of a next page.

schema.title: Response Get Trades V1 Account Trades Get

403.description: real_broker_refused: a real broker's account, asked by a user who is not an administrator. broker_unavailable: the real broker has no login up on this site now.

get.description:
The settings form: each setting by its dotted settings path, in the order of the settings classes, with how the form
shows it, the value the file on disk sets (else its default, else null), its options and bounds, and whether it
applies only at a restart. The AI prompts of instructions.yaml are fields at their settings paths, such as
ai.system_prompt.

schema.title: Response Get Settings V1 Admin Settings Get

422.description: A settings file does not parse (settings_refused); the problem says where.

put.description:
Writes every change into its settings file in place, every other line, comment and key as it was, opens the app on
the new files, writes them and runs on them at once, when the app starts with them and the password is the
administrator's own; or refuses with nothing written and the app as it was. A change to the value its field shows
is skipped, and changes that change nothing write nothing. Runs that started earlier finish on the settings they
started with. The answer is the form after the save.

schema.title: Response Save Settings V1 Admin Settings Put

403.description: A save without the password (password_required), or with a wrong one (password_refused).

409.description: The server reloaded its settings after the request started, or another save wrote a file first (settings_conflict); nothing saved.

schema.title: Response 422 Save Settings V1 Admin Settings Put

422.description: The app would not start with the new settings (settings_refused, with the problems at their settings paths), or a change names no field of the form or cannot be written in place (settings_edit_refused).

429.description: Too many wrong passwords from this address (sign_in_throttled); Retry-After says when.

get.description: Every user, oldest first. No administrator sees another user's data: this is the directory only.

schema.title: Response List Users V1 Admin Users Get

patch.description:
Changes a role, deactivates or reactivates a user, or sets a new password. A deactivation or a new password ends
every session of the user at once; their data stays, and a run of theirs already running finishes.

409.description: No active administrator would remain; nothing saved.

get.description: The signed-in user with their permissions, which the app reads to show the administration pages. 401 when signed out.
My settings: the AI models the site offers, its default, and the one the user's runs use. 401 when signed out.

put.description:
Chooses the AI model of the user's next runs, or null for the site's default. A run already running keeps its model.
A model the site stopped offering later leaves the choice saved, and the runs use the site's default meanwhile.

422.description: The site does not offer that model; nothing saved.

post.description: A new user with the role user: 403 while registration is closed, 409 for a taken username or email, 429 past the limit.

First use only: the administrator, who takes over the data of the single-user version. It needs the setup code the
server printed on its console at start (403 otherwise), so the first visitor of an exposed server cannot claim it.
409 once a user exists. The app then signs in like any user.
Sets the session cookie. 401 for a wrong name or password, one message for both; 429 past the attempt limits.
Ends this browser's session and clears its cookie. Signing out twice is fine.

get.description: What the web app shows first: the first-time setup while no user exists, then sign-in, with registration while it is open.
The user's saved backtests, newest first: the site keeps the newest accounts.saved_backtests of each user.

schema.title: Response Get Backtests V1 Backtests Get

post.description:
Replays the user's active technical strategy over the period, day by day with the live trading rules, and answers
the backtest, saved for the user. A stock is decided on its technical score alone, as a run decides a stock the AI
is not asked about; a decision made after one session's close fills at the next open. It asks no AI, touches no
account and never orders. The answer comes when the replay is done: seconds, longer for the first one after a start.

422.description: invalid_request: a field of the body does not validate, and `detail` lists each one. backtest_period_unavailable: the period reaches outside the days the site's daily history can replay, or holds no session; `detail` says which days a backtest may cover.

get.description:
What the user may ask a backtest for: the strategy it would replay, and the inputs of the longest one the site's
daily history allows at the live settings. A backtest reads only sessions the site already holds.
One saved backtest of the user, with its days and trades. Another user's id answers 404.

404.description: The user has no saved backtest of that id.

post.description: Deletes one saved backtest of the user. Another user's id answers 404 and deletes nothing.

404.description: The user has no saved backtest of that id.

get.description:
How many sessions of TWSE and TPEX closes the server's open-data archive holds, and how many the built-in strategies
need. A public site's runs read their daily history from it, so they find no candidate until it holds enough. Public.

The credit the Open Government Data License v1 requires wherever the site shows the TWSE and TPEX open data or what
it computes from it: each providing agency with the datasets the site reads, the license's notice, and the
license's name and address. Public.

Whom the site serves, personal or public, and what that allows, from the one table of each audience's capabilities.
Realtime quotes also need this runtime's Shioaji login, which a personal site may lack. The web app shows only what
the site can do by it; the server still refuses the rest. Public.

The latest session's advancers, decliners and unchanged stocks in the TWSE and TPEX daily listings, each with the
exchange's own change, and the same per industry with the average change in percent. Public.

503.description: The exchange listing could not be loaded.

get.description:
One market index's completed daily bars, oldest first, from the daily history the stock pages share: the history
cache of the exchanges' own reports on a personal site, else the open-data archive. Public. Like a stock's history, it
fetches no realtime quote.
The latest session's most traded stocks in the TWSE and TPEX daily listings, with that session's bar. Public.

schema.title: Response Get Most Traded V1 Market Most Traded Get

503.description: The exchange listing could not be loaded.

get.description: Listed and OTC stocks whose code or name matches, best first, each with its latest official close. Public.

schema.title: Response Search Stocks V1 Market Stocks Get

503.description: The exchange listing could not be loaded.

get.description:
One stock's completed daily bars, oldest first, from the history cache the workflows share. Public. It fetches
no realtime quote: the latest bar is the last settled session's close.

One stock's financials from the server's open-data archive: each archived quarter's revenue, gross profit,
operating income, net income and EPS of the year to the quarter's end, its total assets, liabilities and equity at
the quarter's end and its book value per share, and each archived month's revenue with its changes. Amounts are in
thousands of TWD, per-share figures in TWD and changes in percent; a figure the company's industry format does not
report is null. Both lists are empty for a stock the archive holds nothing of. Public.

The owner's active strategy applied to the stock exactly as a run applies it, with each indicator's value at every
